subject: Middle School Lottery Information Session
overview: District administrators presented the 2022 middle school lottery process and timeline to fifth-grade families, explaining the methodology used to balance student populations between the Andrews and McGlynn schools.

items.title: Introductions and Meeting Overview
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Cushing and Director Ricciardelli welcomed families and established the framework for the information session regarding middle school assignments.

items.title: Lottery Rationale and Policy
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent explained that the lottery system was created to correct racial and socioeconomic imbalances between the Andrews and McGlynn Middle Schools.

items.title: Program-Level Assignments and Exceptions
items.summary: Administrators clarified that students requiring specific English Learner or specialized Special Education programs are assigned to the school housing those services regardless of the lottery.

items.title: Sample Lottery Walkthrough
items.summary: The Superintendent presented a statistical breakdown of a sample school to illustrate how various student categories, including buffer seats and sibling preferences, affect the number of seats available in the general draw.

items.title: Buffer Seats for English Learners
items.summary: The district reserves seats at the McGlynn Middle School to accommodate the high volume of English Learner students who enroll throughout the academic year.

items.title: Lottery Timeline and Notification Process
items.summary: Staff reviewed the schedule for the March sibling forms, the April 5 virtual lottery drawing, and the mailing of official assignment letters on April 12.

items.title: Middle School Programming and Joint Activities
items.summary: Administrators described the unified sports teams, shared club fairs, and efforts to maintain curriculum consistency between the two middle school campuses.

items.title: Special Education Lottery Procedures
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Cushing explained that students with IEPs whose needs can be met at either school enter a separate lottery to ensure they are divided equally between buildings.

items.title: Public Q&A
items.summary: Officials answered questions regarding socioeconomic balancing data, transportation for after-school activities, and guest policies for school dances.
